newsitem.title: Italy: Pope celebrates 77th birthday, says "23 more to go".
newsitem.headline: Pope celebrates 77th birthday, says "23 more to go".

text.p: A healthy-looking Pope John Paul marked his 77th birthday on Sunday joking that although he was approaching his "sunset" he hoped to live to be 100.
Thousands of people turned out to fete the Pope at a Rome parish in a crowded, working class neighbourhood where he said a morning mass and later for his blessing in St Peter's Square.

Despite recent health problems, the Pope appeared in good form at both appearances, joking and smiling broadly as he expressed gratitude for the thousands of birthday greetings that have arrived from around the world.
Seventy-seven red balloons went up into the air at the Rome parish where the Pope was grilled by neighbourhood children.
"On our birthday our mothers tell us to promise to do something. What do you promise to do?" a small boy asked him.
"To behave better," he joked.
The Pontiff then used the occasion to reflect on his life, including the twists of fate that brought him from a small town in Poland to be the leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics.

He noted that he was born between five and six p.m. in 1920 and that it was also betwen five and six p.m. on October 18, 1978 that cardinals chose him to be the first non-Italian Pontiff in 450 years.
He neglected to mention that it was also between five and six p.m. that he was shot and nearly killed by a Turkish gunman in St Peter's Square on May 13, 1981.
"These are the moments of my life's history. Everyone has a personal history that leads to eternal life," he said.
"I, after 77 years, am closer to this sunset (than you are)," he told them. "You are still children."
When the children chanted the Polish birthday refrain "sto lat" he said: "Do you know that 'sto lat' means 'may you live 100 years'? Well then, I've got 23 to go. Let's hope so. Time passes."
Later, thousands of people in a festive St Peter's Square sang Happy Birthday in various languages and held up banners.
The Pontiff, who was born on May 18, 1920 in Wadowice, Poland, has suffered a series of health problems in recent years and undergone several operations.
He is also widely believed to be suffering from Parkinson's Disease or a related ailment that causes his left hand to shake.

Despite calls from his doctors to slow down his busy schedule of foreign travel, this year is proving one of the most hectic for some time for the Pontiff, whose globetrotting has earned him the nickname of the "Pilgrim Pope".

He has visited Sarajevo, the Czech Republic and Lebanon in recent weeks and is due to make a gruelling 11-day trip to his homeland in June. More visits are scheduled to Paris in August and Brazil in October.
Heads of state and ordinary Catholics sent messages for the occasion.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in a birthday message that the "fruitful apostolic mission of the Holy Father to all corners of the world, such as the recent visits to Sarajevo and Beirut, is...a constant reminder to work for peace, justice and brotherhood between peoples".
President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro also sent a message of best wishes in the name of the Italian people praising the Pope's mission of "truth, liberty and justice".
"May your voice continue to be one of comfort and encouragement for Italy and for the whole world," he said.
